title: Interim Shaft Seal Kit for the Green System Engine Driven Pump
abstract: Interim seal kit for the green system engine driven pump shaft, released to stop hydraulic fluid loss into the accessory gearbox drive pad while a full case redesign was developed.

sections.reason: Hydraulic fluid was found in the accessory gearbox drive pad cavity on a growing number of aircraft, at a rate of 1.4 events per 1000 flight hours against a fleet target of 0.2. The path was the green system engine driven pump shaft seal, which was suffering from the pressure spikes generated when the landing gear and the flaps are operated together on a short turnaround. Fluid loss was gradual and did not produce a low-level warning before the reservoir reached the refill line, so the first indication was usually a wet drive pad found at a transit check. A full pump case redesign was already in work but was more than two years from release, so an interim answer was required.
sections.description: The shaft seal assembly is replaced by a two-element kit consisting of a pressure-balanced primary seal and a scavenge lip seal that returns leakage to the case drain rather than to the drive pad. The pump solenoid BE759984-33 is retained and the anchor nuts AES818405K5 at the mounting flange are renewed at every kit installation. The pump valve D2910110251872 is unchanged. The kit is installed with the pump on the aircraft, working from zone 123 with the fan cowl open, and the case drain line is flushed before the pump is returned to service. The solenoid FIN 16GG and the clamp FIN 280GG8 are disturbed during access and are re-secured to the torque values on drawing D29101190176 issue B.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.3 kg per pump position. No electrical load change. The kit is fully interchangeable and can be fitted to any pump of the affected standard. Fluid loss into the drive pad was reduced but not eliminated, so the kit carries a repeat check of the drive pad cavity every 1200 flight hours, which is why it was always described as an interim measure. Component maintenance content for the pump was re-issued and the AMM removal and installation tasks for ATA 29-10 were amended.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through a single bulletin, with an elapsed time of about six hours per pump at line maintenance. Kits are supplied against firm orders with a ten week lead time, and both pump positions of an aircraft are normally brought to the kit standard in the same visit.

type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; interim solution offered to the in-service fleet only

title: Interim Shaft Seal Kit for the Green System Engine Driven Pump

issue.reason: The interim standard is formally closed: no further kits are supplied and the mixed period that attrition conversion creates is stated in the dossier.

abstract: Interim seal kit for the green system engine driven pump shaft, released to stop fluid loss into the accessory gearbox drive pad and now formally closed, with the fleet converting to the redesigned case by attrition.
